about: The editor's spoken feedback on the studio, piece by piece, as deck@the-ultimate-insider wrote it down. Recorded first, then prioritised: a note here is not a request until deck sends it.
session: 29 October 2026, from 14:25 UTC, the editor reviewing the lab live

ui.note: Review pages must present, not just link: use the whole screen width (no empty margins), show the piece itself on the page instead of making him click through to it.
Each review must say plainly what decision is asked of him, and show the feedback he has already given.
A way to replay each piece and skip forward and back (scrub), to see how it works; some pieces may need to go faster.
Every piece should show its ID (E01, E02, ...) really big, so he always knows which one he is on.
Move between pieces directly (E01 to E02 and on) without going back to the programme to find the next one and its small 'the piece' link.
The programme's cards should show what he consumes: a screenshot or two of the latest version, how many versions there are, the title and a line; not the data and sources.
The piece, explainer and review links belong in a secondary navigation on the piece's own page.
Replaying a piece today means reloading the page: replay and scrub are needed.

pieces.verdict: keep both v1 and v2 in the talk: they show different views
likes: v2 (reach in motion) is very interesting; he can tell the story with it, each step
v1's list on the left: chat model, one tool, and so on, which he can keep reading
v3: merge both: v2's visualisation with v1's step list on the left
too much red: vary the colours
pieces.priority: later: not now; first collect feedback on all pieces, then decide what to put in and what to fix first

pieces.verdict: into the talk: v3 (by what it touches) and v1 (the rows beside the drawing); not v2 (the individual dots are not needed)
likes: v3: 'the blast radius is everything its grant reaches', the mandate, the excess grouped by what it touches: a really lovely way of seeing it
v1: the rows beside the drawing
v4: too much red: shades of different colours
the sector labels (credentials, ...) are tight and overlap the last numbers: make it a little bigger
show how dangerous each capability is: some are not critical, some are very critical; map that (with a source, not invented)
pieces.priority: later, except putting v3 and v1 in the talk

deck.note: Put the studio animations into the talk, with start and stop, so he sees them in action in the flow: they are already better than the current slides. Fifty slides is fine.
